product: McDonalds-branded QSR meals - burgers, chicken, fries, McCafe and desserts - via drive-thru, delivery, self-order kiosks and app (digital 66pct of Q2 2026 sales). Value platforms Econequequi and McXMenos, FIFA World Cup 2026 sponsorship, plus Super Mario Galaxy and Stranger Things licenses drove demand (2026-08-13).
demand: Volume-led with mix. Q2 2026 comparable sales +15.3pct on the strongest guest traffic of six quarters, transactions up in all three divisions, plus higher average check in Brazil and SLAD; digital sales +25pct (2026-08-13). Q1 2026: volume in NOLAD/SLAD, check in Brazil/SLAD (2026-05-20).
pricing_power: Food and Paper inflation, especially in NOLAD/SLAD (flagged in 4Q25), plus payroll and occupancy cost growth, FX devaluation, and loss of value-platform pricing power would compress margins. Q2 2026 margin relied on lower Food and Paper and G&A (2026-08-13); reversal of Brazil tax benefits would also dent results.
competition: Yes - many cheaper local QSR, street-food, bakery and informal vendors across Latin America sit below McDonalds price points; Chinese-origin chains are only a marginal presence. Arcos defends with value platforms (Econequequi, McXMenos) rather than owning the low-cost tier (2026-05-20).
market_strategy: CEO Luis Raganato promised efficiency and monetization: committed to finding additional efficiencies in growth investments over the next few years (2026-03-19); to build on the foundation and capitalize on competitive advantages (2026-05-20); to keep monetizing guest connection (2026-08-13). Guidance: open 105-115 units and capex USD275-325m in 2026.
